APPROACH: New _eigh_clust_full runs mega_eigh_clust_split on the FULL n=512 matrix (k=n) -- the brief-35 cluster kernel already handled k=608/768 reduced blocks; adapted it to a full-matrix solve with the same torch tensor-core WY back-transform + per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback. Routed via a spectrum-FLATNESS probe: participation-ratio PR>=200 (lapdense_even PR~284; low-rank-winnable decaying spectra PR<165 are caught by the low-rank path first) AND a _twolevel_mask exclusion (frac<0.5) so the clustered shape (PR=512 but A^2~I) stays on its faster two-level path.

TRIAL ARC: t1 wire full-n cluster C=2 (shape11 208->146ms BUT stole shape9 clustered -> geomean REGRESSED 38688) -> t2 exclude 2-level (shape9 restored, geomean 33705, -1.9%, WIN) -> t3 C=3 (shape11 147->132ms, geomean 33382) -> t4 C=4 REGRESSES (shape11 167ms) so C=3 is the knee -> t5 bisIters 45->30 (shape11 130ms, geomean 33175, BEST) -> t6 tf32x3 back-transform REGRESSES (Ozaki overhead on B*512*512) -> t7 3xTF32 orth gate NEUTRAL -> t8 FINAL revert orth to FP32 (geomean 33171-33210, clean).

PROFILE (shape11, C=3): mega_eigh_clust_split_k = 105.5ms = 81.5% of the shape; back-transform GEMMs + gate ~20ms fixed tail. The kernel is dominated by the SERIAL per-column tridiagonalization (512 columns, each a GLOBAL v/p round-trip + cluster.sync).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not fully explored, all would deepen this win):
(1) PANEL/BLOCKED tridiag inside the cluster kernel (brief-35 open dir 1): the 105ms kernel is ~all serial per-column tridiag with a global round-trip per column. A panel (NB reflectors) tridiag with the trailing two-sided update as a torch tensor-core GEMM would cut the cluster.sync + global-exchange count ~NB-fold -- the single biggest remaining lever, but a major CUDA rewrite SHARED with the k=608/768 paths (risks shapes 4/10), so I did not attempt it late in the brief.
(2) Faster cross-CTA v/p exchange (race-free DSMEM instead of global staging+threadfence) -- brief-35 open dir 2, ~1-2ms/call.
(3) The ~20ms back-transform+gate tail: the eigen-gate af@Q (TF32) + orth Q^T@Q (FP32) are ~12ms at b640 -- a cheaper gate (e.g. reuse a partial GEMM, or a probe-subset gate) could shave it.
(4) C=3 was best of {2,3,4} but the cluster-size/NT/bisIters interaction was only swept 1-D; a joint sweep (esp _MEGA_CLUST_NT, currently 512, vs C) might find a better operating point for the full-n b640 regime specifically.
(5) shape 8 (rankdef, 93ms) stays on low-rank k=384 (optimal since exact rank 384<512); the full cluster path would be MORE work there so it was correctly not routed. But shape 6 (mixed512) has a dense subset already peeled to low-rank -- whether the flat-dense matrices in mixed512 would benefit from the cluster path over low-rank k=352 was not probed.
